reader: Claude Opus 5.5, in the audit's lead session, reading the paper against both AI readings

decisions.text_extraction: Decided by Lukas Wallrich on 2026-11-04: a reading checked against a differently extracted copy of the same paper counts like any other. If the correction fixes an error, it should be made.
decisions.unsure_reader: Delegated by Lukas Wallrich on 2026-11-04 and decided after reading a seeded random sample of 16 fields: when both readers back a change but one is unsure, one more read of the paper decides. Change the value only if the paper contradicts the existing value; keep it if the existing value is defensible. When the readers do not agree on the new value and at least one is unsure, keep the existing value.

sample.population: 74 fields where both readers back the change, at least one is unsure and current FLoRA still holds the old value

row:1927:outcome.reason: The author reads both full samples as not showing the effect and finds it only under low response effort. 'Successful' overstates this.

row:1537:outcome.reason: The authors' conclusion says they could not replicate the behavioural findings, while self-reports did replicate.

row:592:outcome.reason: The authors say the original intellectual dimension is not confirmed in India. The existing quote describes their revised model, not the original.

row:702:outcome.reason: Only two of the four tested gene regions carried through, and the paper refers to genes it did not validate.

row:929:outcome.reason: The author recomputes the original's own series, finds values that do not match its stated procedure, and warns against using its time trends.

row:929:type.reason: The paper recomputes the original's published series from its own spreadsheet and sources, so it is a reproduction.

row:37:outcome.reason: Five gene regions from the original were re-tested. The abstract says one was associated and the other four were not.

row:1858:original.reason: The paper says it replicates its references 17 and 18. The existing original appears only as another reference.

row:2254:original.reason: The paper opens by re-testing Azzi and Ehrenberg (1975) and rebuts the study now on record.

row:2674:outcome_robustness.reason: The claim survives some checks, but the authors' first main conclusion is that the gaps grow where manipulations worked, so similarity cannot be concluded with confidence.

row:2655:outcome_computation.reason: The author classes the results as partially reproducible and the central table reproduces exactly, so 'technical failure' is wrong.

row:313:outcome.reason: The original model reached only marginal prediction at a tenth of its original size. 'Failed' and 'mixed' are both defensible.

row:1246:outcome.reason: The authors give no verdict on the original. They report support on some factors alongside new results, so 'mixed' is defensible.

row:342:outcome.reason: The attention prediction held and the learning benefit did not. 'Failed' is defensible because the authors say they did not replicate the learning result.

row:726:outcome.reason: The authors conclude in accordance with the original and call the main results of the two studies coherent. Changing this would add an error.

row:14:outcome.reason: This audits change over time and gives no verdict on the original, so no value is clearly right.

row:1554:outcome.reason: The abstract says weak support and the discussion counts the effect as replicated. Both values are defensible.

row:577:outcome.reason: The authors say they replicated one association and failed to replicate the other. Previously held only because of how the text was extracted.

row:579:outcome.reason: The authors call their results largely consistent, then name differences in trial time and recall. Previously held only because of how the text was extracted.

row:1162:outcome.reason: The authors call this a strongly inconclusive attempt and not a strong test, which is 'uninformative'. Previously held only because of how the text was extracted.

row:1162:original.reason: Both readers name the study this report replicates. Current FLoRA already holds it.

row:536:outcome.reason: The authors say the direct replication failed while the conceptual replications gave support.

row:536:original.reason: Both readers name the same original. Current FLoRA already holds it.
